subject: USAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB495 — The whole minimum-range table was measured at its boundaries with the pinned compiler (probe p11, --std 2023): BINARY-CHAR SIGNED -128 and 127, UNSIGNED 255; BINARY-SHORT SIGNED -32768 and 32767, UNSIGNED 65535; BINARY-LONG SIGNED -2147483648 and 2147483647, UNSIGNED 4294967295; BINARY-DOUBLE SIGNED -9223372036854775808 and 9223372036854775807, UNSIGNED 18446744073709551615 - every one stored and displayed exactly, so "any integer value of n within the specified range shall be expressible in the given usage" holds for all eight rows. "integer numeric data items" - PicInfo.BinaryItem synthesizes Scale 0 and the item is PICTURE-less (§13.16.3 SR8). "held in a binary format suitable for the machine" - ByteForm Binary, two's complement, widths 1/2/4/8 (probe p50 reads 0x01 0x02 for BINARY-SHORT 258 and 0xFF 0xFF for -1 and for UNSIGNED 65535). The SIGNED NESTING ("any number that may be expressed as BINARY-CHAR shall also be expressible as BINARY-SHORT …") follows from the 1/2/4/8 width ladder and was measured directly (probe p12: -128 through BINARY-SHORT, -32768 through BINARY-LONG, -2147483648 through BINARY-DOUBLE, all exact). "The implementor may allow a wider range" is OPTIONAL and deliberately not provided - docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 item 206 documents that each usage holds exactly the GR12 minimum, and probe p31 shows the boundary is enforced rather than silently wrapped when a checking phrase is present (`COMPUTE BCU = BCU + 100` from 200 raises SIZE ERROR; the same for a signed BINARY-CHAR at 200). unit:BinaryCapacityTests pins the same boundaries at the runtime level with values computed from the table. Introduction gate: COBOL0900 below COBOL-2002 (probe p44 at --std 85), silent at 2002/2014/2023. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The range table itself is genuinely met - I re-measured all sixteen boundary values independently and every one is exact - but the rule's FIRST sentence, 'The usages binary-char, binary-short, binary-long, and binary-double DEFINE INTEGER NUMERIC DATA ITEMS that are held in a binary format', fails for the second of the usage's two legal declaration shapes, and the adjudicator's probes (p11, p12, p31, p50) only ever declared the item at 01 level with the usage on its own entry. SS13.18.60.4 GR1 (cite-checked) says a USAGE clause specified at a group level 'applies only to each elementary item in the group', SS13.18.60.3 SR2 expressly permits the same usage on both the group entry and the subordinate entry, and SS13.16.3 SR8 (cite-checked) forbids a PICTURE clause 'for an item whose usage is binary-char, binary-short, binary-long, binary-double, float-short, float-long, float-extended, index, ...' - so `01 GB USAGE BINARY-SHORT.  05 AB.` describes an elementary 2-byte integer item. MEASURED with the pinned compiler: AB has FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH 0, with NO diagnostic and exit 0 - it is silently a zero-length group, not a binary item, so NO value in the GR12 range is expressible in it. The SAME program compiled with the SR2-explicit form (`05 AB USAGE BINARY-SHORT.`) gives 2, which proves the group-level USAGE clause is accepted and that only the GR1 INHERITANCE path is broken; and `01 GI USAGE INDEX.  05 AI.` correctly gives 8, so the compiler HAS the picture-less-usage resolution machinery (DataBinder.ResolveIndexItems) and built it for USAGE INDEX only. Worse than silent: `01 GB USAGE BINARY-SHORT UNSIGNED.  05 AB.  ...  MOVE 65535 TO AB` makes the COMPILER CRASH - unhandled System.NullReferenceException at MoveEmitter.ConvertSource, exit 1 - at --std 2002 and --std 2023 alike. NOTE FOR THE REGISTRAR: this is ONE root defect (picture-less group-usage inheritance implemented for INDEX only) shared with my GR13, GR14, GR15 and GR21 verdicts - one fix closes all five; do not count it as five independent defects. Everything else in GR12 holds: BINARY-CHAR -128/127/255, BINARY-SHORT -32768/32767/65535, BINARY-LONG -2147483648/2147483647/4294967295, BINARY-DOUBLE -9223372036854775808/9223372036854775807/18446744073709551615 all stored and displayed exactly at --std 2023 AND --std 2002; the signed nesting measured through all three widenings; widths 1/1/2/2/4/4/8/8; COBOL0900 x8 at --std 85. The cited test conformance:cases/13.18.60-USAGE/binary_usage is spec-derived (its header cites SS13.18.60) but pins only the BINARY-CHAR row's three boundaries plus three interior values - it never declares the usage at a group level. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/Model/PicInfo.cs#PicInfo.BinaryItem; src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/Model/PicInfo.cs#PicInfo.Truncation; src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Values/Numeric/CobolNum.cs#WrapBinary; src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Values/Numeric/CobolNum.cs#InBinaryRange; docs/CONFORMANCE.md#DOC-A.1-206 || CLOSED 2026-09-09 by kb/Work PB495 (landed). The REFUTED paragraph above names the ONE root it shares with GR13, GR14, GR15 and GR21 -- "picture-less group-usage inheritance implemented for INDEX only" -- and says in terms that one fix closes all five. That fix is landed: 13.18.60.4 GR1 is now implemented as an EQUIVALENCE rather than as a special case, over ONE derivation of an elementary item's effective usage (its own USAGE clause, else the nearest enclosing one) feeding the group-header shed, the leaf's representation and every 13.18.60.3 screen through the same code the written-clause path runs. So `01 GB USAGE BINARY-SHORT. 05 AB.` is a 2-byte binary item and `01 GF USAGE FLOAT-LONG. 05 AL.` an 8-byte floating-point one, not the ZERO-LENGTH cells measured above, and the MOVE that crashed the compiler with an unhandled NullReferenceException in MoveEmitter.ConvertSource runs. RE-MEASURED, both spellings, whole matrix: a (usage x picture x arm) sweep of 138 cells found 108 DIFFERING on the pre-fix tree 39479e19 and 0 differing after, and the equivalence is now a drift theory over the whole Usage enum rather than a set of cases. The spec-derived witnesses are the two new goldens: conformance:cases/13.18.60-USAGE/pb495_group_usage_applies_to_each_leaf prints W=1 2 4 8 4 8 8 (binary-char/-short/-long/-double, float-short, float-long, index) with GRP=4 for a two-leaf BINARY-SHORT group and CTL=2 for the written-clause control, and conformance:cases/13.18.60-USAGE/pb495_group_usage_standard_float prints W=4 8 2 2 with F=16777216 16777217 -- 2**24+1 rounded by binary32 and held exactly by binary64, the sharpest single discriminator between the two interchange formats -- and N=-32768 65535, which is GR21 sentence 2's SIGNED/UNSIGNED length identity together with the UNSIGNED phrase reaching the leaf from the group entry. Everything the REFUTED paragraph credits as already holding is unchanged.
